The main takeaway from our work is that
, while it is true that there are some significant differences in the prices of different types of animals, the overall pattern of livestock prices is very similar to that of grain prices.

, while there was a general upward trend in the price of livestock over the period, the price of each animal was subject to a different pattern of fluctuation, with no one animal showing any clear relationship to any other animal.

, while it is possible to find evidence for the existence of a livestock market in England during the thirteenth-century, it is not possible to say that the market was efficient in a manner that would be recognizable to modern economists.
